articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft patches 167 vulns including a SharePoint zero-day and 'BlueHammer' weakness in Windows Defender. April 2026's Patch Tuesday is serving more holes than a cheese convention.

articles.title: Attackers are cashing in on fresh 'CopyFail' Linux flaw
articles.summary: Fresh 'CopyFail' Linux kernel flaw gets weaponized faster than you can say 'reliable root exploit.' CISA warns it's already being abused in the wild.

articles.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw (CVE-2026-23918) Enables DoS and Potential RCE
articles.summary: Palo Alto's PAN-OS gets pwned via critical buffer overflow (CVE-2026-0300, CVSS 9.3). Unauthenticated RCE because apparently firewalls need their own fires put out.

articles.title: DAEMON Tools Supply Chain Attack Compromises Official Installers with Malware
articles.summary: Apache HTTP/2 serves up CVE-2026-23918 with a side of potential RCE (CVSS 8.8). The web server that powers half the internet just gave everyone a heart attack.

articles.title: Microsoft Edge Stores Passwords in Process Memory, Posing Enterprise Risk
articles.summary: Trellix source code gets breached, giving attackers the blueprint to their security products. It's like handing burglars the plans to your alarm system.

articles.title: Your work apps are quietly handing 19 data points to someone
articles.summary: French 15-year-old allegedly breaches France Titres, exposing 12-18 million government records. Teenagers: breaking governments faster than they break curfew.

articles.title: EFF Submission to UK Consultation on Digital ID
articles.summary: EFF fights the 'turnkey totalitarian state' that NSA whistleblower William Binney warned about. Because surveillance empires outlast the politicians who build them.

articles.title: Shut Down Turnkey Totalitarianism
articles.summary: EFF and 18 orgs tell UK policymakers to fix root causes of online harm instead of breaking the open web. Revolutionary concept: solve problems instead of censoring them.

articles.title: Kuwait Exports Zero Barrels of Oil for the First Time Since 1991 Gulf War, Monitor Says
articles.summary: OAuth tokens from AI tools and productivity apps are creating persistent backdoors that security teams can't see. Your employees' convenience is attackers' persistence.

articles.title: U.S. government warns of severe CopyFail bug affecting major versions of Linux | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Common workplace apps including Gmail and Teams are quietly leaking 19 data points per user. Your office productivity suite is more like a corporate surveillance suite.
